mike: Heads-up — hitting a goroutine leak in the Go SDK generator when cancelling the ctx concurrently with auth token refresh. Minimal repro in a tiny sample app below.

mike: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()

g, err := client.Generator(ctx, modelID)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }

// simulate cancel right after starting stream
go func() {
  time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
  cancel()
}()

stream, err := g.Stream(ctx)
if err != nil { log.Printf("stream err: %v", err); return }
for tok := range stream.Chan() {
  // never exits in repro if auth refresh races and blocks handshake
  _ = tok
}
```

sarah: Oof. Is this the auth-provider refresh that blocks the initial handshake goroutine?

olga: We think so — our credential provider does blocking I/O during refresh for a few seconds, which can hold the handshake path. If the handshake goroutine hasn't wired up the cancellation/select yet, cancel doesn't interrupt it.

mike: Confirmed. Repro uses a fake GetToken that sleeps ~3s then returns 401 -> refresh. Cancel races with that and the generator stream never observes ctx.Done().

james: Short-term workaround: set a per-handshake timeout in sample apps. But that's rough for DX.

olga: Two possible long-term fixes: 1) make the auth provider API/context usage strictly context-aware so refresh can be cancelled, 2) change generator handshake to select on ctx sooner (or provide an Abort/Close that forces handshake teardown).

mike: API ergonomics question: users expect generator.Stream(ctx) to respect ctx cancellation immediately. Do we prefer adding an Abort() on the generator object or making the handshake accept an explicit handshake ctx option?

james: FWIW python/node SDKs avoid this by ensuring auth refresh funcs take an explicit ctx and by registering cancellation before heavy I/O. Go creds interface currently lacks a single canonical ctx param in our code paths.

dev-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary test run detected gen-stream goroutine leak on private-e2e — creating INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-321

sarah: For parity and DX: we should (a) add context param to credential provider interface, (b) update docs + sampleapp to show correct cancel patterns, and (c) add unit test that simulates slow refresh + ctx cancel.

james: I'll prototype a PR to make GetToken(ctx) required and add a generator.Abort() as a compatibility shim. Will include a sample-app change and a leak detection test. Assigning to self.

mike: Thanks — I'll add a short sample app note in the onboarding README showing the Cancel pattern and linking to the PR once ready.

olga: Also add CI goroutine-leak check for generator e2e tests so we don't regress.

mike: :thumbsup: tagging this for follow-up in the SDK parity triage meeting.
